claims.text: Pre-coating tungsten particles or connected tungsten regions with a thin, uniform WC nanolayer before spark-plasma sintering will improve interfacial bonding relative to direct sintering or vapor-coated tungsten powder baselines.
The WC pre-coating will improve thermal transport relative to the named baselines.
The WC pre-coating will enhance mechanical durability under irradiation relative to the named baselines.
CVD at 600–700 °C can produce a thin, conformal WC nanolayer on tungsten surfaces.
The 600–700 °C CVD window will minimally alter the bulk properties of tungsten.
The WC interlayer effectively wets both tungsten and copper.
A uniform WC interlayer bridges the tungsten–copper interface.
The WC interlayer eliminates interfacial void formation.
The WC interlayer creates strong metallurgical bonds at the tungsten–copper interface.
The WC layer reduces interfacial energy between tungsten and copper.
Reduced tungsten–copper interfacial energy enhances wettability during sintering.
The WC layer mitigates phase separation during processing.
The WC layer acts as a diffusion barrier at the tungsten–copper interface.
The diffusion-barrier action of WC reduces irradiation-induced interfacial degradation.
WC-coated composites will have fewer interfacial defects than composites made by direct spark-plasma sintering or with vapor-coated tungsten powders lacking the optimized carbide layer.
WC-coated composites will have higher thermal conductivity than the baseline composites.
WC-coated composites will retain greater bonding integrity and fatigue resistance under high-heat-flux and irradiation loading than the baseline composites.
